newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Plavsic considers dissolving Serb assembly -- TV.
newsitem.headline: Plavsic considers dissolving Serb assembly -- TV.

text.p: Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic raised the possibility of dissolving the Serb assembly on Thursday in a letter to her government opponents who have demanded she step down, local television reported.

"I ask you to give me your opinion by 3 p.m. on July 3 on the possible dissolution of the people's assembly of the Serb republic," Plavsic was quoted as saying in a letter to Dragan Kalinic, assembly speaker.
The letter cited a constitutional crisis and article 72 of the Serb entity's constitution as the basis for a possible dissolution of parliament, the television said.
Hardliners loyal to indicted war criminal and ex-president Radovan Karadzic were preparing to launch a vote to remove Plavsic at an assembly session scheduled for Friday.
There was no immediate confirmation of the letter from Plavsic's office in the northern town of Banja Luka, where police loyal to the president are guarding her building.
The power struggle in Bosnia's Serb entity between Plavsic and Karadzic's allies erupted over the weekend when the president called for the replacement of the interior minister, a Karadzic loyalist.
